title: Planning questions review
description: Make sure the planning agent is told to ask the user questions as needed. I haven't had any questions in a long time.
plan:
## Problem

The `plan-headless.md` prompt template actively discourages the planning agent from asking questions. Line 28 says "Only include questions if you genuinely need human input to proceed" — this causes the agent to skip questions and produce plans based on assumptions instead.

The bug template (`plan-bug.md`) correctly encourages questions by listing specific categories to ask about and stating "you should almost always have questions."

## Changes

### 1. Update `pipeline/prompts/plan-headless.md`

Replace the current instructions section with stronger guidance that encourages question-asking:

- Remove the discouraging language "Only include questions if you genuinely need human input"
- Add a list of categories the agent should consider asking about (similar to bug template), such as:
  - Scope boundaries (what's in/out of scope)
  - User-facing behavior expectations
  - Integration points with existing code
  - Edge cases and error handling preferences
  - Priority/ordering if multiple sub-tasks
- Add language like: "When in doubt, ask. A short clarification now saves significant rework later."
- Keep the existing JSON structure and checkpoint instructions unchanged

### 2. Verify the code path works

The code in `phases.py:run_planning()` (lines 484-491) already correctly handles questions — when questions are present in the JSON output, it calls `feature.set_questions()` and moves the feature to `requested-input` stage. No code changes needed.

### Files to modify
- `pipeline/prompts/plan-headless.md` — update instructions to encourage question-asking
